queries.query: "large language model" "network configuration" OR "NetOps" OR "network operations"
queries.rationale: Locate work where LLMs are explicitly applied to generate or translate network configurations or NetOps instructions.

queries.query: "LLM" OR "large language model" "network troubleshooting" OR "troubleshoot" OR "fault diagnosis" "AIOps"
queries.rationale: Find empirical studies and tools that use LLMs for network troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, or AIOps-style incident response.
Search specifically for architectures that combine generation, automated validation, and repair for network configs (generate–validate–repair pattern).

queries.query: "network configuration verification" OR "configuration verification" "Batfish" "Veriflow" "Anteater" "Header Space Analysis"
queries.rationale: Retrieve foundational and recent work on deterministic/ formal network verification tools used to validate properties of configurations and possible integration points for LLM outputs.
Identify existing benchmarks/datasets and their limitations for evaluating LLMs/AIOps in networking contexts and locate referenced suites like TSNBench/6G-Bench/OpsEval.
Find literature addressing hallucination/incorrect factual generation by LLMs in operational contexts and mitigation techniques applicable to NetOps.
Locate research on LLMs using external tools (verifiers, simulators) and self-correction loops relevant for safe NetOps workflows.
Search for prompt-injection and adversarial prompting threats and defenses in operational contexts, particularly where erroneous configs could be induced.
Find work on adversarial perturbations, robustness testing, and red-teaming of LLMs with relevance to NetOps safety evaluation.
Identify evaluation environments and testbeds used to execute or validate generated network configurations and their suitability for LLM-driven experiments.

queries.query: "metrics" "network configuration correctness" OR "policy compliance" OR "reachability" OR "semantic correctness"
queries.rationale: Collect papers defining operationally meaningful correctness metrics (reachability, isolation, policy compliance, performance) for evaluating generated configs.
Retrieve methodological guidance for reliable evaluation of LLM interventions, including paired designs, uncertainty quantification, and failure-mode analysis.
Search literature on human–AI collaboration, decision handoff strategies, and operator trust for LLM-assisted network operations.
Locate recent work on agentic LLMs, orchestration frameworks, and safety controls relevant to autonomous NetOps agents.
Survey adjacent domains (IaC, CloudOps, Kubernetes) where LLMs are used to synthesize configurations to transfer lessons, failure modes, and mitigations to NetOps.
Find case studies and incident analyses of misconfigurations (LLM-caused or otherwise) to build a taxonomy of operational failures and real-world impact.
Identify formal synthesis and correct-by-construction methods that can be used as mitigations or validators for automatically generated configs.
Find public datasets and corpora of real network configurations useful for training/evaluating LLMs and for constructing realistic tasks.

inclusion_criteria: Primary sources (peer-reviewed papers or arXiv preprints) with verifiable metadata (title, authors, year, venue/identifier).
Empirical or methodological work that evaluates, validates, or instruments LLMs/AI for operational tasks relevant to NetOps (configuration, troubleshooting, change planning, repair).
Papers on formal/deterministic network verification, emulation/testbeds, and metrics that can validate generated configurations.
Benchmarks, datasets, and tool releases (GitHub/Zenodo) tied to networking or AIOps evaluation.
Work describing failure modes, safety/robustness, prompt-injection/adversarial threats, or mitigations applicable to NetOps.
Neighboring-domain studies (CloudOps, IaC, software config synthesis) with clear transferrable lessons to NetOps.
Standards, RFCs, and authoritative tools/docs (IETF RFCs, Batfish docs) when they inform validation criteria.
exclusion_criteria: Opinion pieces, blog posts, or marketing materials that lack technical details or verifiable empirical evidence (except where industry postmortems provide factual incident data).
Non-English sources unless an authoritative English translation is available.
Papers unrelated to operational network tasks (pure NLP/model-internal optimization papers without application to config/NetOps).
Pre-lock internal or unpublished development artifacts that cannot be independently verified.
Works that only report superficial Q&A-style LLM benchmarks about networking knowledge without operational execution or validation.
date_rationale: Prioritize literature from 2020–2026 to capture the rapid LLM/agentic-AI developments while including earlier foundational networking verification and emulation work (e.g., Batfish/Veriflow/Header Space Analysis) irrespective of date. This balances recent LLM-specific methods with established NetOps verification tools and datasets; include pre-2020 foundational works as necessary.
